verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद । शरणं पालयानस्य यो धर्मस्तं ब्रवीहि मे ॥१॥
verses.english: Yajnavalkya said, I have already spoken to you of the science of the Sankhyas. Hear now as I truly describe the science of the Yogins as heard and seen my me, O best of kings. are

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              महान्धर्मो महाराज शरणागतपालने । अर्हः प्रष्टुं भवांश्चैव प्रश्नं भरतसत्तम ॥२॥
verses.english: There is no Knowledge like that of the Sankhyas. There is no power like that of Yoga. These two prescribe the same practices, and both are considered as capable of leading to Liberation.

verses.sanskrit: शिबिप्रभृतयो राजन् राजानः शरणागतान् । परिपाल्य महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥३॥
verses.english: Those men who not blest with intelligence consider the Sankhya and the Yoga systems to be different from each other. We, however, O king, regard them as one and the same, according to the conclusion to which we have arrived.

verses.sanskrit: श्रूयते च कपोतेन शत्रुः शरणमागतः । पूजितश्च यथान्यायं स्वैश्च मांसैर्निमन्त्रितः ॥४॥
verses.english: What the Yogins have in view is the very same which the Sankhyas also have in view. He who sees both the Sankhya and the Yoga systems to be one and the same is to be considered as truly conversant with the principles that ordain the universe.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              कथं कपोतेन पुरा शत्रुः शरणमागतः । स्वमांसं भोजितः कां च गतिं लेभे स भारत ॥५॥
verses.english: Know, O king, that the vital airs and the senses are the chief instruments for practising Yoga. By only regulating those vital airs and the senses, Yogins go everywhere at their will.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              शृणु राजन्कथां दिव्यां सर्वपापप्रणाशिनीम् । नृपतेर्मुचुकुन्दस्य कथितां भार्गवेण वै ॥६॥
verses.english: When the gross body is destroyed, Yogins, gifted with subtile bodies possessed of the eight Yoga powers wander over the universe, enjoying all sorts of happiness, O sinless one.

verses.sanskrit: इमर्थं पुरा शत्रुः पार्थ मुचुकुन्दो नराधिपः । भार्गवं परिपप्रच्छ प्रणतः पुरुषर्षभ ॥७॥
verses.english: The wise have, in the scriptures, spoken of Yoga as giving eight sorts of power. They have spoken of Yoga as gifted with eight limbs.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मै शुश्रूषमाणाय भार्गवोऽकथयत्कथाम् । इमां यथा कपोतेन सिद्धिः प्राप्ता नराधिप ॥८॥
verses.english: Indeed, O king, they have not spoken of any other sort of Yoga. It has been said that the practices of Yogins, excellent as those are of two sorts. Those two sorts, according to the characteristics described in the scriptures, are practices endued with attributes and those freed from attributes.

verses.sanskrit: मुनिरुवाच । धर्मनिश्चयसंयुक्तां कामार्थसहितां कथाम् । शृणुष्वावहितो राजन् गदतो मे महाभुज ॥९॥
verses.english: The concentration of the mind together with the regulation of the vital airs. O king, is one sort. The concentration of the mind along with subjugation of the senses, is of another sort. The first kind of Yoga is said to be that possessed of qualities; the second kind is said to be that freed from qualities.

verses.sanskrit: कश्चित्क्षुद्रसमाचारः पृथिव्यां कालसम्मितः । विचचार महारण्ये घोरः शकुनिलुब्धकः ॥१०॥
verses.english: The, again, Regulation of the Vital air is Yoga with qualities. In Yoga without qualities, the mind, freed from its functions, should be fixed. Only the regulation of the vital air which is said to be endued with qualities should, in the first instance, be practised, for, O king of Mithila, if the vital air be exhaled without mentally thinking upon a definite image, the wind in the neophyte's system will increase to his great injury.

verses.sanskrit: काकोल इव कृष्णाङ्गो रक्ताक्षः कालसम्मितः । दीर्घजंघो ह्रस्वपादो महावक्त्रो महाहनुः ॥११॥
verses.english: In the first period of the night, twelve ways of suppressing the vital air are recommended. After sleep, in the last period of the night, other twelve ways of doing the same have been laid down.

verses.sanskrit: नैव तस्य सुहृत्कश्चिन्न सम्बन्धी न बान्धवाः । स हि तैः सम्परित्यक्तस्तेन रौद्रेण कर्मणा ॥१२॥
verses.english: Forsooth, one endued with tranquillity, of controlled senses, living in retirement, rejoicing in one's in one's own self, and fully conversant with the meaning of the scriptures, should fix his Soul.

verses.sanskrit: नरः पापसमाचारस्त्यक्तव्यो दूरतो बुधैः । आत्मानं योऽभिसंधत्ते सोऽन्यस्य स्यात्कथं हितः ॥१३॥
verses.english: Removing the five faults of the five sense, viz., (withdrawing them from their objects of) sound, form, touch, taste, and scent, and removing those conditions called Pratibha and Apavanga, O king, of the Mithilas, all the senses should be fixed upon the mind.

verses.sanskrit: ये नृशंसा दुरात्मानः प्राणिप्राणहरा नराः । उद्वेजनीया भूतानां व्याला इव भवन्ति ते ॥१४॥
verses.english: The mind should then be fixed on Consciousness, O king; Consciousness should next be fixed on Intelligence, and Buddhi should then be fixed on Nature.

verses.sanskrit: स वै क्षारकमादाय द्विजान् हत्वा वने सदा । चकार विक्रयं तेषां पतङ्गानां जनाधिप ॥१५॥
verses.english: Thus merging these one after another, Yogins meditate on the Supreme Soul which is One, which is freed from Darkness, which is Immutable and Infinite and Pure and without defect, and without blemish, who is Eternal Soul, who is unchangeable, who is Indivisible, who is without decay and death, who is everlasting who is above decrease, and which is Immutable Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: एवं तु वर्तमानस्य तस्य वृत्तिं दुरात्मनः । अगमत्सुमहान्कालो न चाधर्ममबुध्यत ॥१६॥
verses.english: Listen, now, O king, to the marks of one that is Yoga. All the marks of cheerful contentment that are his who is sleeping in contentment are seen in the person, that is in Samadhi.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य भार्यासहायस्य रममाणस्य शाश्वतम् । दैवयोगविमूढस्य नान्या वृत्तिररोचत ॥१७॥
verses.english: The person in contemplation, the wise hold looks like the fixed and upward flame of a lamp that is full of oil and that burns in a spot where there is no air.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कदाचित्तस्थाय वनस्थस्य समन्ततः । पातयन्निव वृक्षांस्तान्सुमहान्वातसम्भ्रमः ॥१८॥
verses.english: He is like a rock which is incapable of being moved in the last by even a heavy downpour from the clouds.

verses.sanskrit: मेघसंकुलमाकाशं विद्युन्मण्डलमण्डितम् । संछन्नस्तु मुहूर्तेन नौसाथैरिव सागरः ॥१९॥
verses.english: He is incapable of being moved by the sound of couchs and drums, or by songs, or the sound of hundreds of musical instruments beat or blown together. Even this is the characteristic of one in contemplation.

verses.sanskrit: वारिधारासमूहेन सम्प्रविष्टः शतक्रतुः । क्षणेन पूरयामास सलिलेन वसुन्धराम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: As a man of cool courage and determination, while going up a flight of steps with a vessel full of oil in his hands, does not spill even a drop of the liquid if terrified and threatened by person armed with weapons, so the Yogin, when his his mind has been concentrated and when he sees the Supreme Soul in contemplation, does not, of account of the entire stoppage of the functions of his senses at such a time, move in the slightest degree. Even these should be known to be the marks of the Yogin while he is in contemplation.

verses.sanskrit: ततो धाराकुले काले सम्भ्रमन्नष्टचेतनः । शीतार्तस्तद्वनं सर्वमाकुलेनान्तरात्मना ॥२१॥
verses.english: While in contemplation, the Yogin sees Brahma which is Supreme and Immutable, and which is situated like a burning Effulgence in the midst of thick Darkness.

verses.sanskrit: नैव निम्न स्थलं वापि सोऽविन्दत विहङ्गहा । पूरितो हि जलौघेन तस्य मार्गो वनस्य च ॥२२॥
verses.english: It is by this means that he acquires, after many years, Liberation after renouncing this inanimate body. Even this is what the eternal Shruti says.

verses.sanskrit: पक्षिणो वर्षवेगेन हता लीनास्तदाभवन् । मृग-सिंह-वराहाश्च स्थलमाश्रित्य शेरते ॥२३॥
verses.english: This is called the Yoga of the Yogins. What else is it? Knowing it, they who are gifted with wisdoin consider themselves as crowned with Success.

verses.sanskrit: महता वातवर्षेण त्रासितास्ते वनौकसः । भयार्ताश्च क्षुधार्ताश्च बभ्रमुः सहिता वने ॥२४॥
verses.english: All the dwellers of the forest were stricken with fear for that dreadful storm and rain. Terrified and hungry, they roved through the forest in small and large packs.

verses.sanskrit: स तु शीतहतैर्गात्रैर्न जगाम न तस्थिवान् । ददर्श पतितां भूमौ कपोतीं शीतविह्वलाम् ॥२५॥
verses.english: With limbs benumbed by cold, the fowler, however, could neither stop where he was, nor could he move. While in this state he saw shepigeon lying on the ground, benumbed with cold.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वाऽऽर्तोऽपि हि पापात्मा स तां पञ्जरकेऽक्षिपत् । स्वयं दुःखाभिभूतोऽपि दुःखमेवाकरोत्परे ॥२६॥
verses.english: Beholding the birds, the sinful person, though he himself himself was in better circumstances, picked her up and put her in a cage. Himself afflicted with distress, he did not hesitate to overwhelm a fellow-creature with painful affliction.

verses.sanskrit: पापात्मा पापकारित्वात्पापमेव चकार सः । सोऽपश्यत्तरुखण्डेषु मेघनीलवनस्पतिम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: Indeed, through force of habit alone, the wretch committed that sin even at such a time. He then saw in midst of that wood a huge tree blue as the clouds. no

verses.sanskrit: सेव्यमानं विहङ्गौघैश्छायावासफलार्थिभिः । धात्रा परोपकाराय स साधुरिव निर्मितः ॥२८॥
अथाभवत्क्षणेनैव वियद्विमलतारकम् । महत्सर इवोत्फुल्लं कुमुदच्छरितोदकम् ॥२९॥
verses.english: It was the refuge of numberless birds seeking shade and shelter, as if it were placed there by the Creator for the behoof of all creatures like a good man in the world.

verses.sanskrit: ताराढ्यं कुमुदाकारमाकाशं निर्मलं बहु । घनैर्मुक्तं नभो दृष्ट्वा लुब्धकः शीतविह्वलः ॥३०॥
verses.english: Soon the sky cleared and became spangled with myriads of stars appearing like a splendid lake smiling with blooming lilies.

verses.sanskrit: दिशो विलोकयामास विगाढां प्रेक्ष्य शर्वरीम् । दूरतो मे निवेशश्च अस्माद्देशादिति प्रभो ॥३१॥
verses.english: Looking at the clear sky, rich with stars, the fowler began to advance, still trembling with cold. Seeing the sky cleared of clouds, he looked around and finding that he had already been benighted, he began to think.

verses.sanskrit: कृतबुद्धिर्द्रुमे तस्मिन्वस्तुं तां रजनीं ततः । साञ्जलिः प्रणतिं कृत्वा वाक्यमाह वनस्पतिम् ॥३२॥
verses.english: My house is at a great distance from where I am!-He then thought of passing the night under the shade of that tree.

verses.sanskrit: शरणं यामि यान्यस्मिन् दैवतानि वनस्पतौ । स शिलायां शिरः कृत्वा पर्णान्यास्तीर्य भूतले । दुःखेन महताऽऽविष्टस्ततः सुष्वाप पक्षिहा ॥३३॥
verses.english: Having said so, he spread some leaves for a bed, and laid himself down on it, placing his head on a stone. In spite of his being overwhelmed with affliction, the man soon fell asleep.
